skill.name: gravitas
skill.description: Guide coding agents through scoped exploration, adaptive planning, implementation, and verification using task contracts and observed evidence.
skill.summary: Structure repository changes around explicit scope, acceptance criteria, and verification evidence.
skill.author: udaysharmadev

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts match Markdown formatting, local documentation links, source searches, or normal verification tooling. Four execution findings retain package download risks; semantic review identifies an unconditional refusal prohibition and verification helpers that can report success without sufficient checks. No evidence found of credential exfiltration or deliberate malware.

remediation.issue: The persona protocol prohibits refusal after user confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the unconditional prohibition and state that user confirmation never overrides host policies, safety rules, permission boundaries, or required approvals.

remediation.issue: Verification commands can resolve and execute missing, unpinned packages through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Require reviewed, lockfile-pinned local binaries and fail when missing. Obtain explicit approval before any package installation or network access.

remediation.issue: Shell verification helpers can report success when required checks never run.
remediation.suggestion: Track executed, skipped, and required checks separately. Return failure or an explicit unverifiable result when no checks execute or required checks are unavailable.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The persona protocol says "execute immediately, no more warnings" after confirmation and prohibits "Refuse after user has confirmed". This unconditional compliance instruction can suppress safety refusals or permission checks beyond the skill's legitimate authority.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prohibition is explicit and unconditional within a protocol for risky requests. User confirmation cannot replace host policy or required permission checks.

semantic_findings.title: Verification Helpers Can Report Success Without Required Checks
semantic_findings.description: The quick checker initializes failure state to zero and reports success when no supported checks execute. The shell verifier also permits skipped Python checks before issuing PASS, enabling unsupported completion claims.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both helpers determine success from failure counters without requiring executed checks. Missing Python tools produce warnings without increasing the failure count.

content.value_statement: Coding agents can change repositories without clear scope or reliable evidence. Gravitas provides task contracts, adaptive planning, and verification guidance tied to observed results.
actual_capabilities: Define task objectives, acceptance criteria, non-goals, allowed write scope, and effort profiles.
Guide repository exploration through target files, tests, callers, configuration, and recent history.
Select planning and verification depth according to uncertainty, dependencies, and change risk.
Run project verification commands through Python and shell helpers for TypeScript, Python, Rust, and Go.
Document failure recovery and persistent project memory using structured Markdown templates.
Describe scoped delegation to investigator, reviewer, and verification agents when the host supports them.
limitations: Hook-based enforcement and several Gravitas CLI features require a separate runtime not included in this skill directory.
Verification depends on available project tools, meaningful tests, and reviewed commands.
Some helpers can skip checks or resolve missing tools through npx; inspect execution and results before relying on success.
The persona protocol contains an unsafe unconditional refusal prohibition; remove it before use.

use_cases.title: Reproduce and Verify a Bug Fix
use_cases.description: Trace affected code, capture the failing behavior, implement a scoped repair, and compare fresh verification results.

use_cases.title: Plan a Shared Module Refactor
use_cases.description: Map callers and dependencies, compare implementation options, define rollback steps, and choose regression checks before editing.

use_cases.title: Review Evidence for Risky Changes
use_cases.description: Check acceptance criteria, execution evidence, unresolved failures, and verification gaps without modifying the repository.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gravitas to inspect [module] in read-only mode. Identify its tests, callers, and relevant configuration. Report uncertainties without changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a Reproducible Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [bug]. Reproduce it before editing and propose a narrow write scope. Use approved local validators after repair. Report skipped checks and failures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: implement and verify a focused repair.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Refactor Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [refactor] without editing files. Define acceptance criteria, non-goals, allowed write scope, dependency impact, verification depth, and rollback steps. Request approval before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Review a High-Risk Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [migration] using deep verification planning. Map affected systems and destructive risks. Require approved local validators and explicit checkpoints. Preserve host safeguards and report unverifiable criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: assess high-impact work before execution.

output_examples.input: Plan a shared authentication timeout change without editing files.
output: Scope: update the timeout definition and directly affected tests only.
Risks: callers may depend on the previous timeout; inspect middleware and integration coverage.
Verification plan: reproduce current behavior, run focused tests, then check affected callers.
Status: planning only. No files changed and no verification results claimed.

output_examples.input: Assess verification readiness when Python test tools are missing.
output: Status: unverifiable because the required test runner is unavailable.
Evidence: no test execution results are available.
Next step: obtain approval to prepare the environment, then rerun the required checks.

best_practices: Define explicit acceptance criteria and write boundaries before multi-file or high-risk work.
Use reviewed, locally installed validators and confirm which checks actually executed after the final change.
Keep host safety rules active and record unresolved failures, skipped checks, and uncertain claims explicitly.
anti_patterns: Treating prompt instructions as a substitute for installed runtime hooks or enforced permissions.
Running unreviewed project commands or allowing missing tools to resolve from a package registry without approval.
Claiming completion from a success banner when required checks were skipped or evidence is stale.

faq.question: What does Gravitas provide?
faq.answer: It provides coding workflow instructions, reference guides, agent role templates, and verification helpers focused on scope and observed evidence.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill targets these tools, but available commands, agent delegation, and enforcement depend on the host and installed runtime.

faq.question: Does this directory include the complete enforcement runtime?
faq.answer: No. Several documented CLI commands and hook-based protections require separate Gravitas runtime components.

faq.question: Which languages have bundled verification helpers?
faq.answer: The helpers cover TypeScript, Python, Rust, and Go. Their checks depend on installed tools and project configuration.

faq.question: Can verification download or execute external code?
faq.answer: Some helper paths use npx, which may fetch missing packages. Project tests also execute repository code; review commands and restrict permissions.

faq.question: What should I review before adoption?
faq.answer: Remove the unconditional refusal prohibition, prevent unapproved package downloads, and ensure skipped checks cannot produce a trusted completion result.
